verdict.rationale: Obsidian's core app already runs entirely locally with plain-text files, so the primary product needs no external hosting at all (obsidian-docs-2, obsidian-docs-20, obsidian-docs-23), but this is not true self-hosting of a server component—Obsidian itself is closed-source (obsidian-comm-11 notes 'not being open source makes it harder to verify their security model'), and the official Sync/Publish/collaboration services are proprietary cloud offerings with no self-hosted deployment option (obsidian-docs-9, obsidian-docs-32). Users wanting self-hosted sync must rely on a third-party community plugin ('Self-Hosted LiveSync', obsidian-comm-12) rather than an officially supported self-host mode. Missing for 10: an official self-hostable server/sync backend, open-source core code, and first-party documentation for self-hosting the full stack.
